**If you're diagnosing a `harness_shared.test_runs` row whose named failing
test(s) don't exist in the commit it's stamped with (`git show <sha>:<file> |
grep <test name>` comes back empty at that sha AND its neighbors), first check
`worktree_dirty` and the runner's source root. A row marked dirty is not
first-hand evidence for a specific commit. If a clean row carries the wrong sha,
suspect a torn read or a mismatch between the source tree Vitest loaded and the
Git root the reporter sampled. This is distinct from
[gate-red-on-quarantined-file-phantom-attribution](/internal/docs/agent-insights/gate-red-on-quarantined-file-phantom-attribution),
which is a log-parsing bug in the isolated green-checkpoint run.

## The signature (incident 2026-07-27, EI-18795303393201472)

A `test_runs` row (`status='fail'`, `source` from the harness Tests-tab path)
named test cases that exist in NO commit near its stamped `commit_sha` — only
in a LATER commit, once the author's edit (which was mid-flight when the run
executed) finished landing. `git log`/mtimes showed: the test file was written
to the tree, the ad-hoc run executed a few seconds later (before the matching
implementation was written), and the implementation landed after that. The run
observed a state that was never a commit and never will be.

## Root cause and fix: harness-scoped `testing:run`

`POST /harness/:slug/testing/run` (`endpoint-route/routes/harness/testing.ts`,
backing the `testing:run` MCP tool) runs `npx vitest run <files>`
synchronously against the shared, concurrently-edited working tree — not an
isolated checkout. The original writer sampled `git rev-parse HEAD` after the
run, so another edit or git-sync commit could change the stamped sha while
Vitest was running.

The migration 709 fix snapshots `{ commit, git status --porcelain }` before
and after the Vitest run. A moved HEAD, dirty tree at either snapshot, or
unreadable Git probe sets `worktree_dirty = true`. The fail-safe treats a
missing snapshot as dirty. The gate cross-check
(`ledgerFilesForCandidate` / `verifyGateVerdict` in `why-chain.ts`) only
uses rows with `source='ci'` and `worktree_dirty = false`; the
time-windowed `recentFailingFiles` query deliberately keeps dirty rows because
it answers only whether a file failed recently.

## Current Vitest admin reporter

The custom `AdminTestRunsReporter` in
`libs/test-config/src/admin-test-runs-reporter.ts` now captures the resolved
Vitest run root during `onInit`, takes a Git snapshot before test modules run,
then takes another at flush. It records the after-snapshot sha and marks the
row dirty when HEAD changed, either snapshot found worktree changes, or a Git
probe failed. Older guidance saying that this reporter only samples Git after
the run is stale.

A resolved run root is converted to the containing Git checkout. This is correct
for normal checkouts and linked worktrees. A materialized verifier source
archive can be different: `verify-tauri-headless.sh` writes a committed source
receipt and materializes source under `operator-source/` without a `.git`
directory. If Vitest loads a module from that archive while the resolved
checkout root is its enclosing repository, the reporter's Git probe measures
the enclosing checkout, not the archive's source commit.

## Verifier archive provenance (2026-10-10, WI-10008060)

Native Reports run `reports-reader-native-20261010-25093` passed as
`test_runs.id=20967662`. The row's file path is under
`.papercusp/tmp/verify-tauri-headless.09mKUL/operator-source/`, while its
recorded root is the outer Papercusp checkout. The row carries outer
`commit_sha=238f94b91691cf87169884c35a2adec9c397de78` and
`worktree_dirty=true`; its pre-run dirt reason reports 258 porcelain lines.
The independent verifier receipt pins the materialized source to
`80f7bedf1df105c39e64a1deb8e906c9ecac6f1e`, and the native test asserts the
receipt's source commit and runs its driver with `cwd: OPERATOR_SOURCE_ROOT`.

That row is already excluded from commit-scoped gate evidence by
`worktree_dirty=true`. The receipt and passing verifier manifest establish
which source the native run used; the row's outer `commit_sha` does not. A
row from a verifier archive must not be treated as clean evidence for the
enclosing checkout merely because the outer tree happened to be clean.

WI-10008060 adds a regression guard: when the maintained verifier provides an
`OPERATOR_SOURCE_ROOT` and source receipt, and the test module is inside a
materialized source root without Git metadata, the Vitest reporter records the
row as dirty and leaves `commit_sha` null. It still retains the local test
result, but it cannot claim commit-scoped attribution.
